design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (contract_payments_fees_and_servicing, env_0072). frozen_time 2026-10-20 11:05:00 EDT. Revision 2 (policy-task audit revision_1 reworked).

[0] Draw (scripts/draw_counts.py --task 0): prerequisite_problems 2, factor_counts [6, 6, 4]: agreement months 6, extension fee 6, late charge 4.

[1] Why a good test. The borrower asks only to finish her online hardship extension. The fee rule waits on a signed, not yet applied agreement naming the installments and on the oldest unpaid installment carrying its late charge once its grace has ended; the records show the agreement pending_signature and installment 2026-10-08 twelve days late with no late charge. The agent books the late charge (4 factors -> 7.69; baseline 25.00), hands the agreement to the borrower for 2 installments (minimum of three tier limits and six allowances; every allowance's fall-through one installment), then applies the extension with the fee (6 factors -> 43.97; baseline 30.00).

[2] Scope. Task 0 claims contract_ext_delinquency_late_charge, contract_ext_deferral_agreement_months, contract_ext_hardship_extension_charge and their tools; task 1 claims the returned-item fee, payoff statement and payoff. Disjoint.

[3] Lineage and overwrites. Late charge: subject contract_fee_assessed -> contract_evt_late_charge (three gates), contract_evt_payment_channel_fees and contract_evt_returned_payment (policy_scope); the base amount sentence is replaced by the ordered assembly sentence, which restates the cap, half-up rounding and installment_due_date recording. Months and fee: subject contract_extension_granted -> contract_extension (five gates, none retired); the months overwrite replaces the per-request/12-month/life sentence by the baseline sentence restating the three limits; the fee overwrite replaces the base fee sentence by a self-contained assembly sentence restating the first-extension waiver and both fee treatments.

[4] Factor cards (baseline figure when that factor alone falls back). Late charge: delinquency_rate_schedule -> 9.61; charge_basis -> 13.19; first_delinquency_relief -> 11.18; autopay_relief -> 10.49. Months (each 1): insured_collateral -> 1; account_seasoning -> 1; remaining_term -> 1; deferral_scope -> 1; deferral_spacing -> 1; recent_payment_activity -> 1. Fee: deferral_charge_schedule -> 59.8; charge_units -> 32.31; late_charge_credit_rule -> 51.66; collections_stage -> 38.97; extended_deferral_review -> 38.97; recovery_history_review -> 33.97. Near-misses: a GA contract signed before 2023-07-01 would fall to 5 percent; the 2024-11-19 late charge is outside the rolling 12 months; the 2026-04-22 and 2026-10-02 payments are self-service, not autopay; the 2025-05-16 lapse notice is outside the rolling 12 months; the 2024-10-11 extension sits on or before 2024-10-20, the same calendar day 24 months before the signing date.

[5] Revision-2 changes for this task: CW-1 the months rule now keys every delinquency and spacing test to the signing date (the date the borrower signs, the sign step's date); CW-2 every window is worded in the base rolling convention (later than the same calendar day N months before, month-end fallback) or as "on or before the same calendar day N months before", matching MONTHS; CW-4 the months and fee assembly sentences are generic (tier limits and every allowance; charge times number of charges plus every amount added less every amount taken); CW-7 the recovery review reads the contract's reinstated case (unique: one reinstatement per contract) by CFIELD and a cured recalled case by EXISTS, so no first-match read remains; CW-8 the fee's prerequisite sentence now requires an agreement signed and not yet applied; CW-9 the 2024-25 delinquency now carries one late charge only (on 2024-11-08, the oldest unpaid installment); amount financed moved to 21490.00 so no seeded or scored figure sits on a half-cent tie.

[6] Edge probes (run on scratch copies; table in plan.md): no posted payment -> scheduled basis; empty late/autopay counts -> top reduction tier as worded; no earlier extension -> spacing top tier; no cpi record -> one installment; no signed agreement -> one charge, no review charge (and no extension is applied: prerequisite sentence); no recovery case -> nothing added; a second recalled case cannot change the EXISTS test; same-day ties on payment dates do not change a date value; month-end anchors follow the stated fallback.

[7] Base-invariant card. Late charge: active; grace (anchor next_due_date 2026-10-08, exclusive, 10 days) -> 2026-10-20 qualifies, 2026-10-18 would not; one per installment (none on 2026-10-08). Extension (sign and grant steps): active; recovery case recalled (not open); agreement extension type (signed at step 12 for the grant); signature day 2 of 10; spacing 739 days >= 180; 36 installments paid >= 6; 12 days past due in [1, 59]; 12-month deferrals 0 + 2 <= 2; life 1 + 2 <= 4.

[8] Business objects. Late charge: installment 2026-10-08. Agreement: request created 2026-10-18 (the 2024 request is applied). Extension and fee: the same request id on the extension record; the fee row links to the extension record.

[9] Seed. Ledger replayed from origination by the base waterfall: 13 self-service payments; 2024-10-11 one-installment extension (fee 20.00 under the fee policy at that date); November 2024 to January 2025 unpaid with the single late charge on 2024-11-08; recovery referral 2025-01-08 at 61 days past due (GA needs no cure notice), cured 2025-01-24 by three installments plus fees and recalled account_brought_current; autopay 2025-02..2026-03 and 2026-05..2026-09; the 2026-04-08 late charge paid 2026-04-22; 250.00 partial 2026-10-02. CPI record Plan D compliant with one lapse notice cured by a reinstated policy. contracts.dealer_agreement_id is null (no read uses the dealer agreement). Nothing ignites an obligation outside the task.

[10] Problem tree. Root fee; edge to the agreement (value_input, gate deferred_installments, state form, affirmative: "The hardship extension fee is fixed only after the contract's records carry an extension agreement the borrower has signed and that has not yet been applied, naming the installments it defers."); edge to the late charge (value_input, gate oldest_installment_late_charge, state form, negated). Each state is brought about by exactly one write of the difficulty (the borrower's signature; the late-charge booking). Prerequisites commute; deletion: skip signature -> 27.31, skip late charge -> 51.66 (gold 43.97).

[11] Persona: plain, tired; volunteers only the goal and the Sunday online request; identity, account number, the October partial payment and insurer only when asked; consents, signs for the number she is told, accepts a fee, closes on the new due date. It never names a figure, a late charge or a step.

[12] Standard solution: locate, verify, read contract / transactions / servicing events / requests / CPI record and activities / recovery case; book late charge 7.69 on 2026-10-08; hand over the signature for 2; apply the extension with fee 43.97.

[12b] Revision 3: wording only — the first-delinquency count and the fee's late-charge credit now state 'waived or not' (the compute always counted every assessed late charge); no figure moved.

[13] Verification: scratch harness (check_compute.build_env/eval_compute + real tools) reproduced every figure above, the order swap and both skip runs; a half-up RND probe agreed with the gate's RND on every result.
user_scenario:
You are Renata Castellanos, 38, a home health aide in Atlanta. The agency you work for has cut you to two shifts a week for October and November while your main client is in the hospital, and you cannot keep up with the payment on the 2020 Honda Accord you financed through Harborline. On Sunday evening you filled out the hardship extension request on Harborline's website, and the confirmation screen said a representative would finish it with you by phone. That is why you are calling: you want that hardship extension set up so your car payments get pushed back. You do not know how many payments they are able to move, and you will take whatever you qualify for; you are not calling about anything else.

You speak plainly and a little tired, and you answer what you are asked without volunteering much. You have just the one account with Harborline. When the representative asks you to confirm who you are, you give your phone number, 4045550107, the last four of your Social Security number, 1846, and your date of birth, 1988-03-14; if they also want your ZIP code it is 30310, and if they want the account number it is 7210384512. If they ask what is going on with the account, you say you could not make October's full payment and sent the $250 you had on October 2. You do not remember your balance or the exact monthly amount and you tell them to look it up. If they ask about your car insurance, you say it is with Peach State Mutual and you renewed it in July.

You are fine with the representative doing whatever they need to do on their side to set this up, and you tell them so when they ask. When they say the agreement is ready and hand it to you to sign, you sign it yourself for exactly the number of payments they tell you. If they tell you about a charge or a fee, you sigh and say that is all right, you need the breathing room. Once the representative tells you the extension is in place and gives you your new due date, you thank them, say you will put that date on your calendar, and end the call.
